steps.say: Bladder exstrophy starts with a membrane that breaks too early. The cloacal sheet fails to gain muscle reinforcement from the sides, and the weak sheet bursts before the sixth week of pregnancy. The open bladder turns out onto the belly wall, and the whole lower midline fails to close behind it.
steps.tx: Exstrophy begins when the **cloacal membrane** (early lower midline sheet) is not reinforced by **lateral mesoderm** (side-wall tissue ingrowth) and ruptures before the **6th week** (sixth gestational week), everting the open bladder onto the abdominal wall while the entire lower midline stays open behind the premature rupture.

vis.alt: Paediatric urology diagram including congenital reconstructive conditions.
vis.caption: Exstrophy belongs with paediatric reconstructive conditions needing staged repair. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: The defect follows a fixed pattern. Findings include an open bladder plate, a gaping pubic joint with wide separation, split tummy muscles, an open urethra on top of the penis, and a low belly button. The bony ring gapes, the floor has no anchor, and continence cannot develop without rebuilding.
steps.tx: Anatomy comprises an open exposed **bladder template** (bladder plate), splayed symphysis with wide **pubic diastasis** (pubic gap), divergent rectus muscles, **epispadias** (dorsal urethral opening), and low-set umbilicus. The bony pelvis gapes, the pelvic floor lacks anchorage, and continence cannot develop without reconstruction.

vis.alt: Sagittal penile diagram including epispadias among inspected lesions.
vis.caption: Epispadias as the urethral component of the exstrophy complex. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Classic repair runs in three timed stages. Bladder and belly wall closure with bone cuts on both sides happens in the first seventy two hours of life. Penis repair follows at one to two years, and bladder neck rebuilding completes the sequence at four to five years.
steps.tx: **Classic staged repair** (three-stage sequence) closes bladder and abdominal wall with bilateral **pelvic osteotomy** (pelvic bone cuts) in the first **72 hours** (seventy two); epispadias repair follows at **1 to 2 years** (one to two); bladder neck reconstruction by **Young-Dees-Leadbetter** (neck tubularization technique) completes it at **4 to 5 years** (four to five). Each stage builds on the last, and delay compromises the next.

rows: Each stage builds on the last

steps.say: Bone cuts are what allow slack closure. Cuts through the back, front, or socket of the pelvis on both sides are mandatory whenever closure happens after seventy two hours, swinging the pubic bones together without pulling. Without bone release the soft tissues rip apart, and the whole closure fails.
steps.tx: **Bilateral pelvic osteotomy** (both-sided pelvic bone cuts: posterior iliac, anterior innominate, or horizontal periacetabular) is mandatory beyond **72 hours** (seventy two) to bring pubic bones together in **tension-free closure** (suture line without pull). Without bone mobilization soft tissues tear under strain and the closure fails.

rows: Posterior iliac, anterior innominate, or periacetabular

steps.say: One operation can do everything together. Complete primary repair closes the bladder, fixes the penis, and rebuilds the neck in the newborn period in a single sitting. It swaps one big newborn operation for the three stage sequence, in units experienced enough to do it safely.
steps.tx: **CPRE** (**complete primary repair**, Mitchell technique or **complete primary repair**) accomplishes bladder closure, epispadias repair, and bladder neck reconstruction together neonatally. The **Mitchell technique** (single-stage neonatal exstrophy repair) swaps one major newborn operation for the staged sequence, in units experienced enough to do it safely.

rows: A centre experienced enough for safety

steps.say: The Kelly operation gives continence another way. It frees the bladder neck, pelvic floor, and sphincter ring and sets them in normal place around the urethra, restoring continence without needing to narrow the neck itself. Dryness comes from restored shape rather than deliberate blockage.
steps.tx: The **Kelly procedure** (anatomical outlet reconstruction) rebuilds bladder neck, pelvic floor, and external **sphincter complex reconstruction** (sphincter ring repositioning) around the urethra, restoring continence without bladder neck tightening. Dryness comes from restored anatomy rather than deliberate obstruction, and the pelvic floor gains a stable anchor for lifelong control.

rows: Bladder neck, pelvic floor, sphincter complex

steps.say: Bladder size decides the final step. A capacity of at least eighty five to one hundred millilitres under anaesthesia is an absolute must before formal neck rebuilding, because a small stiff bladder cannot store at low pressure however good the outlet. Below this line the surgeon holds off and retrains the bladder.
steps.tx: A **bladder capacity prerequisite** (minimum size rule) of at least **85 mL to 100 mL** (eighty five to one hundred millilitres) under anaesthesia precedes formal **bladder neck reconstruction** (outlet tightening operation). A small stiff bladder cannot store at low pressure however good the outlet, so below threshold the surgeon waits, cycles the bladder, and remeasures.

rows: Small stiff bladders cannot store at low pressure

steps.say: Exstrophy bladders carry lifelong cancer risk far above normal. Opened or rebuilt patients carry a lifelong four hundred fold higher risk of gland cancer from glandular change of the exposed lining. Lifelong camera checks with sampling of suspicious patches are therefore part of the repair, not an extra.
steps.tx: Unclosed or reconstructed exstrophy carries lifelong **adenocarcinoma of bladder** (glandular bladder cancer) risk raised **400-fold** (four hundred times), arising from **cystitis glandularis** (glandular metaplasia of the exposed lining). Lifelong camera checks with sampling of suspicious patches are therefore part of the repair, not an extra.

rows: Lifelong cystoscopy with biopsy of patches
Part of the repair, not an afterthought
